_about: The output format your system must produce. Judges read the rendered case file, but this JSON is what gets machine-checked for recall, false-accusation rate and peso reconciliation. Emit both.
_entity_id_format: Prefix entity ids by type: 'RFC:AAAA010101AA1' for a vendor or company, 'EMP:0001' for an employee. Judges match on these strings.
_peso_reconciliation_rule: peso_amount must equal the sum of the cited exhibit amounts within 2%. Amounts are summed PER TABLE and reconciled against the best-matching table, so citing an invoice AND the bank transfer that settled it is not counted as double the money.

seed.description: The estate seed this run was produced from. Same seed must reproduce the same output.

findings.description: Validated accusations only. An empty list is a legitimate result.

entities.description: Prefixed ids. Every entity needs at least one exhibit supporting its involvement.

narrative.description: Plain language. A non-technical judge must be able to follow it unaided.

rule_broken.description: The specific rule or article, e.g. 'SAT Articulo 69-B'. Not a description of a statistical pattern.

peso_amount.description: Must reconcile to the cited exhibits. This is checked.

money_trail.description: Ordered steps, each citing an exhibit_id. Each step's destination is the next step's source; the trail must connect.

record_id.description: Must exist in your estate. Hallucinated ids are detected.

note.description: One sentence: what this record proves.

leads_not_pursued.description: Leads that were investigated and closed without an accusation. This belongs in the body of the case file, not an appendix.

signal.description: Which detector or check pointed you here.

reason.description: Specific to this entity and the evidence examined. Generic text such as 'insufficient evidence' is scored as generic.

deterministic.description: Judges may run your seed twice.
